newsitem.title: USA: NAACP joins outcry against Texaco.
newsitem.headline: NAACP joins outcry against Texaco.

text.p: The National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People (NAACP) joined the outcry against Texaco on Thursday, threatening action against the company following allegations that its officials had planned to destroy evidence in a racial bias lawsuit.
"The NAACP is considering a number of actions to be instituted against Texaco," NAACP president Kweisi Mfume said in a statement.
The association declined to specify what steps it was contemplating.
"We will have more to say in that regard following our discussions with Texaco Chairman Peter I. Bijur," Mfume said.
An NAACP spokesman said he did not know when Mfume was due to talk to Bijur.
Mfume also urged the Justice Department to investigate the company for possible criminal and civil violations.
The government has already launched a probe through the U.S. Attorney for the southern district of New York.

Texaco retained outside counsel to investigate allegations, which were based on a tape laced with expletives and racial insults, that executives in its finance department aimed to destroy documents sought by a government investigation into racial discrimination at the company.
Bijur said Wednesday he had suspended two current employees and the benefits of two retirees allegedly involved in a plan to destroy the documents.
